title: Designing the Cooling System: Wahoo’s CNC Approach
summary: A machined groove and removable sleeve turn cooling into a set of concrete mechanical questions.

sections.title: A compact engine has to manage heat
sections.text:
The Wahoo Racing jetboard project brings a developing engine architecture into a confined product. That makes cooling a mechanical problem as well as a thermal one. Heat must leave the cylinder through a practical path, while the surrounding structure still supports assembly, sealing and service. An attractive jacket on a drawing cannot answer all of those questions.

A29 takes a first construction step. Building on the integrated engine architecture, the accepted digital study explores an external machined groove closed by a separate removable sleeve. It is an experimental upper-cylinder concept. No cooling hardware has been manufactured, and the model does not establish adequate heat rejection.

sections.title: Make the construction accessible
sections.text:
A one-off CNC prototype needs features that can be reached, held and inspected. The proposed arrangement exposes a circumferential groove on the cylinder body before a separately bored outer sleeve covers it. That provides a useful way to investigate cutter access without assuming that a hidden internal passage can simply be manufactured.

The study separates a core, upper and lower lips, a cover and a reference coolant volume. The three host regions describe one intended continuous machined body. They are not three extra purchased parts. The saved working model contains 478 objects and preserves all 473 objects inherited from the supplier-supported M02 assembly. The construction additions are an alternative study layered over the retained reference geometry.

sections.title: A bounded band, not a complete jacket
sections.text:
The current band lies 2–16 mm below the reference deck. Its provisional outer sleeve diameter is 100 mm, compared with the inherited cylinder envelope of 94 mm. That additional diameter is an explicit packaging question for the jetboard. It does not establish clearance inside the hull, where the actual inner structure, access openings and neighboring components still need evidence.

An independent check found approximately 14.96 mm of axial separation from the nearest accepted exhaust aperture. This is a separation between the aperture band and the proposed construction band. It does not clear unknown three-dimensional ducts, prove a safe ligament or establish full-cylinder cooling. The limits of the check are as useful as the number.

sections.title: Editable geometry makes questions testable
sections.text:
The construction remains parametric. A controlled regeneration changed one groove-depth parameter, and independent checking confirmed the expected changes while preserving the inherited source geometry and the cover. That demonstrates reproducible geometry within this limited construction study.

It does not establish structural strength or a thermal solution. A deeper groove may create more space for a reference coolant volume while also reducing material in the host. The engineering task is to evaluate those competing needs using justified loads, material properties and manufacturing limits. Regeneration makes such comparisons traceable; it cannot supply the missing physical assumptions.

sections.title: The details that must come next
sections.text:
A functional concept needs an inlet and outlet, a coherent flow path, sealing surfaces, sleeve retention and a credible assembly sequence. Coolant pressure, flow distribution, boiling margin, expansion and corrosion strategy remain unresolved. Wall thickness, groove corner radii, tool access, stock and workholding also need review. The upper band alone cannot answer what happens around the rest of the cylinder or head.

Materials, liner or coating choices and finish-bore distortion belong in that same discussion. A removable cover can help inspection and service, but its removal path must exist in the eventual installation. None of these requirements is satisfied merely because the study can be saved as editable CAD.

figure.caption: Actual source-derived A29 upper-band construction. Exploded presentation is explanatory and does not establish assembly access, seals or retention.

sections.title: From concept to an engineering decision
sections.text:
The next useful decision is whether this construction deserves further development against alternatives, including open milled channels with covers and drilled galleries. That requires mechanical, thermal, sealing and installation evidence. A30 native inspection and commercial commissioning remain outstanding. No completed native model inspection or commercial run is claimed here.

The Living BOM keeps the concept connected to component definitions without inventing installed quantities. Follow the engineering roadmap as Wahoo moves from numerical research through editable geometry toward a reviewed physical prototype. The achievement is a clearer, inspectable construction question, with its unresolved requirements still visible.
